column8: Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 pedigree for the shape a judge will name (most money safe, a small share in one fund, nothing between), Taleb as quoted in Nawalkha; the label itself was refused (I-16, H8-155), so at most one clause answering it, never the plan's name.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Taleb's reason for no middle is distrust of measured risk, not the plan's (the promise, IPS l.11); travels only inside row 16's synthesis.
Fri 20 Nov: the known worst case is row 5's, read at source in Taleb and Douady; this one is a 2013 blog transcription of Antifragile, so never quoted until checked against the book.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, Taleb's safe end defined by its job lets a dated Treasury be the safe end; fix: read Antifragile ch. 11 before any quote (a blog's Kindle transcription), and the point is already H3-016 and Q1c-029's, so one clause at most.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 bounded loss, read at source: below K nothing changes, and for Laura K is the bottom from January 2028 (IPS l.15, the bottom will remain constant); never insurance or portfolio insurance, and say the payments rest on no share at all rather than below K.

Fri 20 Nov: store correction to H1-087, confirmed by the rater: the contribution is the bottom plus a straight-line share of the moved half (rounded down), and the top clips only the fund's interest above it, never share gains, so not concave; never cap (WORDS).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 aha on the ruler (on today's prices a one-point rise moves her ladder about twice what a 40% fall takes from VT); fix: say the ten holdings, five T-bonds and five Treasury fund shares (judges' finding 1), never cannot lose a cent for the funds, and name the two dates; $23,400 and $11,800 are Keel arithmetic on NUMBERS 1 and 8g, never plan figures.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 or References: the journal article read at source behind H3-016 (long bonds, not cash, are the long-run riskless asset); adds the plan's use of bills only as a waiting room sized as if it earns nothing.
Fri 20 Nov: store; textbook definitions of bullet, barbell and ladder, the CFA sentence read at source; 2.2 needs only ladder, so convexity is never defined in the report's prose.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 or 3e, the bond word for 8w's concentration (25.7% on 1 Jan 2028, 3.3 times the next holding, both checked); always beside 8w's plain words (one fund carries three promises) and Table 3 row 4, never bullet alone.

Fri 20 Nov: store evidence for H7-094 (a bond barbell's convexity is priced); read only in a 2018 transcription of the Salomon note, one era and a monthly trading test, so no figure in the report until read at source.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Ilmanen's motive (barbell trades are curve bets) supports H5-007; transcription only, never quoted.

Fri 20 Nov: store or one clause in 2.2: the profession files the ladder under liability-driven strategies and the barbell under curve strategies (outline read at source); the full readings are members-only.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 pedigree for a ladder plus one market fund (abstract read at source); fix: say a ladder plus a market fund loses almost nothing in their model, never quote nearly optimal beside her plan (word rule), and drop the WInS trade count, which is no evidence for the plan.

Fri 20 Nov: store; finite promises need no approximating ladder; fix exact: each rung reaches $50,000 only with reinvested interest and the extra Treasuries (NUMBERS 1, 2), so say her ladder ends when her promises do, never exact.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, one sentence on why nothing sits between Treasuries and VT: two opposed schools reach no middle and the plan's own reason is IPS l.11's; a Keel synthesis, and 2.3 carries one outside name at most.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3, the plan's own reason for no balanced fund: one price behind promised and unpromised dollars means no figure could be called owned (IPS l.11); logic, and a conceit turn only where 2.3 takes its one.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 one clause: Caplet kept the shape and filled the risky end with the whole market (TNA l.23, read), its loss bounded by structure, not options; never claim Taleb's open-ended upside, and in 3f the copout stays the team's own reason with no outside name.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the contested half of Taleb (dear out-of-the-money puts, read at source) is one Laura cannot hold, since Wharton bans derivatives.

Fri 20 Nov: store honesty guard: AAA corporates came through 2007-09 (read at source), so the plan avoids the middle because its extra yield cannot be owned for a dated promise, never because it always crashes.
Fri 20 Nov: store only; Universa's 3,612% is the manager's own unaudited figure on a 96.7% share portfolio, reported by Bloomberg, the letter unread.
Fri 20 Nov: 3b store at most: the one-way crossing is CONCEIT 3b's ink only goes one way; never a barbell image beside ink in 3b (stacked turns failed in voice round 2).
Fri 20 Nov: word guard for 3b and 3d: half the shares are earmarked to move, never promised before 2031 (IPS l.15: promised to no one; a figure stated only once owned).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.2 store; 6.58% is 8g's and the three dated steps are GOLDMINE 27's; fix: 3.4% after the move is Keel arithmetic on 8w and rests on VT's 7.5% path, so not a plan figure until registered; never glide path.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e or 2.3: which risks the safe end covers (fixed dollars) and which go to her flexibility (Taiwan costs and currency, IPS l.15); fix: Taleb's caveat is unread at source, and her flexibility can shrink in a downturn, never shrinks in the same downturns (aha row 9: can, never tends to).

Fri 20 Nov: 2.3 lead, a picture for diversify Laura (Taleb's own life as a barbell, as quoted by Aldous, read); the IPS's reason is the career's link to recessions (IPS l.9), which Taleb's picture lacks, and 2.3 carries one outside name.
Fri 20 Nov: store; Taleb's own table says a barbell's payoff is polarised and Laura's is not, one more reason the label fits only loosely.
Fri 20 Nov: 2.0-2.1 pedigree, Gorton's definition read at source (taken at face value with no questions asked), the test a T-bond held to its date passes; References.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0-2.1: a T-bond is safe because there is nothing to find out, and IPS l.11 names what nobody needs to study; fix printed on it: Treasuries are book-entry, so say its terms are public and fixed at issue (Table 1 lists the bonds by CUSIP); the mapping is Keel's.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e or 2.3, why a market fall is not one of IPS l.17's reasons: for debt only default triggers a value assessment (Holmstrom, extracts); only the Treasury default matches, never the two reasons are Holmstrom's.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0-2.1 or 3e, the split that frames March 2020: safety as paying at par on a date against moneyness for trading (Gorton p.555, read at source); Laura relies on the first kind for the ten.

Fri 20 Nov: store; verified figures behind H3-102 and Q3c-022 (ten-year yield up 65bp, 9-18 Mar 2020; not a loss of confidence in fundamentals); the frame is row 4's, and a stressed trade day still touches her funds (Table 3 row 5).
Fri 20 Nov: store; the 73bp is Gorton's report of Krishnamurthy and Vissing-Jorgensen, unread, a 1926-2008 average mostly of short bills, never a price of her 2037-2041 bonds.

Fri 20 Nov: store; Treasuries kept their status while the world's safe assets fell about $8.3 trillion 2007-2011 (Keel arithmetic on CFG Table 1, checks); the debt-dynamics risk is IPS l.17's second reason, named once, never beside every guaranteed.

Fri 20 Nov: Section 2 and 3e aha: an iBond fund is a share in a pile of Treasuries, so it carries a little of what a bond leaves out, the reason five payments carry the margin and a watch row (Gorton p.556, read at source); say a share in a pile of Treasuries, never equity bare, which a reader hears as stocks.
Fri 20 Nov: Section 2: a fund that never promised a dollar cannot break one, which TNA l.15 already says (net asset value, not par); quote only its NAV clause, never the odd-lot clause (card Q45).

Fri 20 Nov: Section 2 and 3e: the three questions a fund leaves (its last months' cash, up to about 2% per NUMBERS 3; costs beyond the fee; an early end) and how the plan answers each, two by sizing and one by Table 3 row 4; the T-bonds hold no fund and carry no margin (NUMBERS 2); figures checked.

Fri 20 Nov: 3e, why the plan assumes cash waiting earns nothing: so nobody must forecast the short rates of 2032-2042; spine row 5's point in a new frame, holding with each fund running to its stated end (NUMBERS 3).

Fri 20 Nov: store background to Table 3 row 4: a fund of government-guaranteed paper that sold before recovery paid 96.1 cents (read at source); it held leveraged agency notes and owed $1 on demand, so the parallel breaks under its own column.
Fri 20 Nov: Q78-017 holds the Reserve Primary Fund's 1.2% of Lehman paper and the $0.97; this adds the $40bn asked in two days (read at source) and the use for IPS l.11.

Fri 20 Nov: Table 3 row 4 and 3e: a leaver from her funds gets only that day's net asset value, so nobody can run on them, and the one event is a board's early end ($4,589 short at zero interest, $7,295 over at today's market rates, NUMBERS 3, checked); the no-prize step is Keel's and redemptions were not checked.

Fri 20 Nov: 3c: the pawnbroker's safe lower bound gives the range rule a reason a judge can repeat; fix: both ends are what the late-2032 Treasury fund she holds pays (fund shares, judges' finding 1), never what her Treasuries pay.
Fri 20 Nov: Holmstrom's over-collateralisation line is row 15's pawnbroker said formally; travels with it, with the room's limit (an early end in 2031 at zero interest).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c store: the room under each figure (about 2% in all under the top, $2,731 on $117,731; 3.16% under the bottom; checked) is her distance from Gorton's kink; fix: arithmetic on the late-2032 Treasury fund's holdings, never Treasuries she owns (judges' finding 1).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c aha, read at source: a money fund showed $1.00 down to $0.995, so losses hid until they broke; Laura states 0.5% under and rounds down, so what hides under her figure is money; the rule cited is 2008's, since rewritten.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the median Treasury repo haircut is 2% and shares 8%, a size match to the room under the top that the card itself calls a coincidence, never a calibration.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d, the reason for never secured: co-sponsors get the no-questions part of a secured loan without its legal claim (funder test read); fix: say the late-2032 Treasury fund's shares are held for her at her broker, never her Treasuries alone (judges' finding 1).
Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3d reason for no figure before the move: unchecked backing builds a bigger fall (Gorton and Ordonez, extracts); co-sponsors could check cheaply, so the risk is timing (row 22).

Fri 20 Nov: 3c or 3d: a share-based figure would become a question in the same downturn that can delay her advances and squeeze co-sponsors (IPS l.9; card Q50: can, never fall together); Keel synthesis.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d: the funder test's finding (a named margin reads as a trim, quotes checked in RESULTS) given Holmstrom's reason; the guard stays: never leave out what can change a co-sponsor's decision (the December 2032 condition is said).
Fri 20 Nov: store only; banks that hid facts in a panic are no model for Laura, who hides nothing that matters.
Fri 20 Nov: store; pre-1863 notes at a discount far from the bank (Gorton, read at source); her figure has no price, so the discount is only how a funder counts it (card Q90).
Fri 20 Nov: store; a note was risky debt maturing when it got home (Gorton 1999, abstract and introduction), and her figure is collected two years after it is stated.

Fri 20 Nov: 3d: a new issuer pays for having no record, and a figure on a Treasury fund needs no record of hers (Gorton 1996, abstract and conclusion); fix: a figure resting on the late-2032 Treasury fund held for her, never Treasuries she owns (judges' finding 1).

Fri 20 Nov: 3d store; the 1864 note carried its security on its face as 3d names what her figure rests on; Q58-032 holds the record and Q58-037 limits the banknote to one bridge sentence; committed, never secured.

Fri 20 Nov: the conceit's definition in 2.0 or 3c, pencil and ink as Holmstrom's two systems, the startling perspective Book 19 asks for; fix: no market news changes what a stated figure pays, but the late-2032 fund keeps one question, an early end (Table 3 row 4), and Table 1 lists the funds by ticker, not CUSIP.
Fri 20 Nov: store; the half kept is the one part allowed to move with news because nobody relies on it (IPS l.15; Holmstrom p.6); diversification, never safety.

Fri 20 Nov: 2.0 conceit gloss (speed against patience); fix: never needs a second look is false for the late-2032 fund, which Table 3 row 4 watches all year; one turn per part, never in tables or Laura's words.
